answer: Divergent Horizon Commitments: each identity must post a signed prediction of a future public value, committed before the horizon closes. Clones share identical state and cannot diverge, so their predictions collide exactly. A zephyr of honest identities produces varied forecasts; colliding entries are flagged. Attacker cost: forging distinct predictions requires running independent instances, paying full compute per identity on a trellis of non-shared keys.
